prompts.master:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: anatomically corrected 2D desktop pet rollover sequence sheet, six intermediate drawings, 3 columns by 2 rows, reading order left to right top to bottom. True transparent background, no text, no border, each entire cat fits in its equal cell with padding, no cropping.
Input image1 is the approved initial curled sleep sprite. Input image2 is the approved final supine sleep sprite. Match these EXACTLY in adult fat body proportions, face, coat length, silver-white hair, black/brown dark contour line, blue ornaments, single gold horn, closed sleepy eyes, neutral pale fur color. Same character, same camera, head on left, rump and one tail on right, same scale.
Primary correction: create a continuous natural roll from curled lying belly-down toward lying on its back. The whole rib cage AND pelvis rotate together around the head-tail axis, with a SINGLE continuous oval torso, plausible shoulder and hip joints. Do NOT turn the belly upward while leaving a separate upright rear-haunch ring behind it. There must NOT be two separate torsos. Never put a disconnected paw on the middle of the stomach. Exactly TWO forelegs from the chest on left, TWO short hind legs from pelvis on right. Near and far limbs have distinct consistent identities. A hidden far paw stays hidden until the torso uncovers it. No extra low-left paw after the forelegs have curled onto chest. Fat belly, rounded cheeks, no obvious chin.
Six chronological poses: (1) curled cat has rolled slightly onto its side, head and shoulder rest low left, forelegs starting to fold to chest, rear legs still tucked together at right hip. (2) deeper side sleep: ribcage and pelvis both tilted identically, forepaws fold close together at chest, only one hind foot visible at right because other behind it. (3) roll onto three-quarter back: entire torso tilts together, rounded belly now partly visible, near hind THIGH follows curved pelvis on right and short lower leg bends upward; far hind leg begins emerging BEHIND at upper right. (4) more supine: weight on spine, both bent hind legs attached to right pelvis, two forepaws over left chest, near rear sole rotates gradually toward viewer, no paws growing from center belly. (5) nearly on back: matching final sprite, short hind knees and feet point upward at right, pink pads visible as appropriate, forepaws relaxed on chest, tail lies naturally on ground to right. (6) settled supine very close to input image2, head posture and horn angle approaching that reference.
Clear physical limb attachments, consistent continuous short thick limbs, calm slow small pose increments, no stretching, no noodles, no detached round appendages, no duplicate contour, no ghosting, no fifth leg. These are SIX distinct sequential poses of ONE rollover, not six unrelated variants.
